column4: Depositors lose the truncated remainder when the router deposits into a capped pool
column5: Depositors lose the truncated remainder when the router deposits into a capped pool -- ### Summary `Router.sol` pulls the caller's whole balance and forwards it to `Pool._deposit`, which silently caps the credited amount at `reserveCap - reserveAmount`. The router assumes the full amount was consumed, so it neither refunds nor sweeps the difference and the excess is left sitting in the shared router where the next caller can take it. ### Root Cause The router treats a partially-consumed deposit as a fully-consumed one.

column4: Router is implemented incorrectly and strands funds when the target pool is near its cap
column5: Router is implemented incorrectly and strands funds when the target pool is near its cap -- ### Summary When the pool is close to its reserve cap the deposit path only accepts part of what was transferred in, but the routing contract never reconciles the accepted amount against the transferred amount. The leftover balance is permanently stranded in a contract that belongs to nobody. ### Root Cause A missing reconciliation between the amount pulled and the amount actually credited.

column4: Epoch settlement prices redemptions off a stale oracle reading
column5: Epoch settlement prices redemptions off a stale oracle reading -- ### Summary `Vault.sol:settleEpoch()` reads the cached oracle price written when the epoch opened instead of refreshing it, so an epoch that stays open across a large price move settles every redemption at the old price and pays the exiting holders out of the remaining ones. ### Root Cause The cached price is never invalidated on settlement.

column4: A zero-length epoch skips the pending-withdrawal queue and locks it forever
column5: A zero-length epoch skips the pending-withdrawal queue and locks it forever -- ### Summary `Vault.sol:settleEpoch()` walks the pending-withdrawal queue only while the epoch duration is non-zero, so an epoch configured with a zero duration settles without ever draining the queue and every withdrawal already queued at that point can never be claimed again. ### Root Cause The queue drain sits behind a duration check that a zero-length epoch fails.
